reviews.text: I grabbed this MacBook Neo hoping it would finally replace my old, clunky laptop for my engineering work. At first glance, the device feels incredibly solid and premium in my hands. Specs include the A18 Pro's 6-core CPU, 5-core GPU, and 16-core Neural Engine. I was ready to dive into some heavy coding sessions immediately after unboxing. A 13-inch Liquid Retina display is on board and the base model starts at $599 for 8GB/256GB, with a 512GB option for $699. The screen looks crisp and the performance felt snappy during my initial setup. It's a lightweight 2.7 lb machine with a 90% recycled aluminum body. I started compiling a large dataset expecting this machine to handle the load effortlessly. But then the system froze completely while trying to run a complex simulation. Fanless design ensures completely silent operation via passive cooling. The lack of Touch ID on the base model meant I had to use the Lock Key for every authentication step. The base model starts at $599 for 8GB/256GB, with a 512GB option for $699.

I thought the MacBook Neo (2026) would finally be the perfect upgrade I've been waiting for since it hit the market on March 11, 2026, after being unveiled on March 4. But then I realized that one of the two USB-C ports is limited to slower USB 2 speeds, which really slowed down my workflow when I tried to transfer large files.
